testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When should you watch out for black ice?

options.text: When it is snowing.
When the temperature is below freezing and the road looks wet.
When the temperature is above freezing and there is snow on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the temperature is below freezing and the road looks wet.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice on the road. You can see the road through it. Watch for black ice when it is below freezing and the road surface looks wet.

questions.question: If your vehicle is hydroplaning, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Do not use the brakes.
Put the vehicle in reverse.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle starts to hydroplane, do not brake. Instead, let off the gas and push in the clutch. This helps you regain control.

questions.question: Who conducts the threat assessment for a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: The TSA
The FBI
The CIA

questions.correctAnswerText: The TSA
questions.explanation: The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) conducts the threat assessment for hazardous materials endorsements.

questions.question: When turning, what should you do?

options.text: Signal before you turn.
Turn off your signal just before you start turning.
Signal only if there are vehicles in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you turn.
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal well before you turn or change lanes. Keep the signal on during the turn. Turn it off after the turn is complete, unless your vehicle has self-canceling signals.

questions.question: When exiting a bus, a driver must:

options.text: Never touch the handrail.
Hold onto the handrail.
Move quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold onto the handrail.
questions.explanation: When exiting during the basic vehicle control skills test, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. For a bus, hold onto the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may cause you to fail the test.

questions.question: What is true about hanging meat as cargo?

options.text: It should never be transported by trailer.
It can be an unstable load.
It must be approved by the EPA.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be an unstable load.
questions.explanation: Hanging meat is an unstable load. It has a high center of gravity and swings, which affects how the vehicle handles. Drive carefully with this cargo.

questions.question: When should you do an after-trip inspection?

options.text: Once a week.
Once a month.
After every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: After every trip.
questions.explanation: Complete an after-trip inspection at the end of each trip or work day. Fill out a vehicle inspection report if required.

questions.question: What should you do about broken suspension parts?

options.text: Repair them right away.
Repair them, but not right away.
They cannot be identified.

questions.correctAnswerText: Repair them right away.
questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up the vehicle and keeps the axles in place. Broken suspension parts are very dangerous and must be fixed immediately.

questions.question: In an S-cam brake, friction is created when:

options.text: The brake shoes and linings press against the outside of the brake drum.
The brake shoes and linings press against the inside of the brake drum.
The brake shoes and linings push against each other.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brake shoes and linings press against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: Friction in the brake drum is created when the brake shoes and linings press against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: Which item does NOT need to be on an Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR)?

options.text: Trip origin
Vehicle Identification Number
Number of meals eaten by the driver

questions.correctAnswerText: Number of meals eaten by the driver
questions.explanation: An IVDR must include the distance traveled, fuel purchased, trip origin, destination, and Vehicle Identification Number. The number of meals eaten by the driver is not required.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, where should weight be placed?

options.text: As high as possible.
As low as possible.
As far to the left as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Heavy cargo placed high up makes a vehicle more likely to tip over. Keep weight low to improve stability.

questions.question: Why should cargo be covered?

options.text: To protect people from spillage.
To hide the materials.
To make it more difficult to steal.

questions.correctAnswerText: To protect people from spillage.
questions.explanation: Cover cargo to protect people if it spills and to protect the cargo from weather.

questions.question: When you pull off to the side of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the driver's side door open.
Turn on the emergency flashers.
Wave your arms.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on the emergency flashers.
questions.explanation: Always use your four-way emergency flashers when stopped on the side of the road. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection with two left turn lanes, which lane should you use?

options.text: The right lane.
It doesn't matter which lane you use.
The left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane.
questions.explanation: You may need to swing right to safely make a left turn. Always start your turn in the rightmost left turn lane.

questions.question: During the driving test, what should you do at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is going too slow.
Get out of the vehicle to check for a train.
Do not change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, do not stop, change gears, pass other vehicles, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the railroad tracks.

questions.question: Why should you do pre-trip inspections in the same order each time?

options.text: You will be less likely to forget to check something.
It will be faster.
It is required by law.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be less likely to forget to check something.
questions.explanation: Doing inspections the same way each time helps you remember all the important checks you need to do.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, where should the heaviest cargo go?

options.text: On top of the lightest cargo.
Under the lightest cargo.
At the rear of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under the lightest cargo.
questions.explanation: Heavy vehicles are more likely to tip over. Place the heaviest cargo underneath lighter cargo to keep the vehicle stable.

questions.question: What should you do if the low air pressure warning comes on in a vehicle with air brakes?

options.text: Test the brakes while driving and continue if nothing seems wrong.
Stop driving right away.
Drive with hazard lights on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop driving right away.
questions.explanation: When the low air pressure warning comes on, stop and park the vehicle as soon as possible. You need to stop safely while you still have some braking power.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, how should you begin?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the turn.
Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the turn.
Turn the wheel as sharply as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: Start by turning the steering wheel opposite to where you want to go. Once the trailer starts to turn, reverse the steering direction to follow the trailer.

questions.question: What is required to get a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: Provide fingerprints and pass a background check.
Provide employment history from the last five years.
Provide a list of countries visited in the last 10 years.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide fingerprints and pass a background check.
questions.explanation: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must submit your fingerprints and pass a background check.

questions.question: If your brakes fail while going downhill, why should you decide what to do quickly?

options.text: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go.
The longer you wait, the more vehicles will get out of your way.
The longer you wait, the slower your vehicle will go.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go.
questions.explanation: When your brakes fail on a downhill slope, you must act quickly. The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go and the harder it will be to stop.

questions.question: When it is hard to see and you are driving near other cars, what lights should you use?

options.text: Use high beam lights.
Use low beam lights.
Use only the clearance lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use low beam lights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving near other cars in poor visibility, such as at dawn, dusk, or in bad weather. High beams can make it hard for other drivers to see.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, how are the air tanks arranged?

options.text: Air tanks are shared between both systems.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You must choose which system you are using.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. They share the brake controls, but each system has its own tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: What is true about distracted driving?

options.text: It is not a concern.
It only happens when drivers are physically doing something while driving.
It can happen from mental activities, like daydreaming.
It is encouraged on empty roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can happen from mental activities, like daydreaming.
questions.explanation: Distractions can be physical (like reaching for something), mental (like talking to a passenger), or both (like texting). To avoid distracted driving, pre-program radio stations, plan your route ahead of time, avoid intense conversations while driving, adjust mirrors before leaving, and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving.

questions.question: Where should your vehicle be at the end of a basic vehicle controls skills test?

options.text: In the general area the examiner described.
In the exact position the examiner described.
Within three feet of the position the examiner described.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the exact position the examiner described.
questions.explanation: You must finish each exercise with your vehicle in the exact position the examiner described. If you do not complete the exercise exactly as instructed, you may fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: How can alcohol be removed from your body?

options.text: By exercising.
By drinking coffee.
By waiting.

questions.correctAnswerText: By waiting.
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. The only way to sober up is to wait and let your body remove the alcohol on its own.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It is required in some states.
It shortens brake response time.
It provides better control.

questions.correctAnswerText: It provides better control.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) helps you have better control during hard braking. However, it does not always shorten your vehicle's stopping distance.

questions.question: If you are not sure if the road is icy, what should you do?

options.text: Guess whether the road is icy.
Open your window and feel the side mirror for ice.
Look closely at the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open your window and feel the side mirror for ice.
questions.explanation: If you think the road may be icy but you are not sure, open your window and feel the front of the side mirror, mirror support, or antenna. If ice has formed on these items, the road is likely icy.

questions.question: Is driving at night easier or harder than driving during the day?

options.text: More difficult than driving during the day.
Easier than driving during the day.
Not recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Driving at night is harder because it is harder to see hazards, headlight glare affects vision, and tired drivers are more common on the road at night.

questions.question: What does an air compressor governor control?

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the tanks.
The temperature of the air pumped into the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the tanks.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, the governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: Regrooved tires:

options.text: Should not be used on any vehicle.
Should not be used on the front of a bus.
Should not be used on trucks hauling gravel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not be used on the front of a bus.
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires cannot be used on the front wheels of a bus.

questions.question: Reaching unsafely for a phone while driving is:

options.text: Acceptable if you are alone in the vehicle.
Acceptable if you plan to use a hands-free feature.
Not acceptable, even if you plan to use a hands-free feature.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not acceptable, even if you plan to use a hands-free feature.
questions.explanation: You must keep your phone within easy reach and stay securely in your seat while driving. Reaching unsafely for your phone is dangerous and illegal, even if you plan to use hands-free mode.

questions.question: When approaching your vehicle for a pre-trip inspection, what sign of trouble should you look for?

options.text: A puddle of oil under the vehicle
Inflated tires
Lug nuts that look tight

questions.correctAnswerText: A puddle of oil under the vehicle
questions.explanation: Look under the vehicle for fresh leaks of oil, coolant, grease, or fuel. A puddle of any of these liquids means there may be a safety problem.

questions.question: Foundation brakes are used:

options.text: Only on the front wheels of a vehicle.
Only on the rear wheels of a vehicle.
On every wheel of a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On every wheel of a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are used on every wheel. The most common type is the s-cam drum brake.

questions.question: When stopping, the brake pedal should be:

options.text: Pressed down gradually.
Pressed down quickly.
Pressed down repeatedly, but not held down continuously.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pressed down gradually.
questions.explanation: When stopping, press the brake pedal down gradually.

questions.question: What is reaction distance?

options.text: The distance you travel from when you decide to brake until you actually press the brake pedal
The distance you travel from when a hazard appears until you see it
The distance you travel from when you see a hazard until you decide to brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance you travel from when you decide to brake until you actually press the brake pedal
questions.explanation: Stopping distance is the sum of three distances: perception distance, reaction distance, and braking distance. Reaction distance is how far you travel between deciding you must brake and actually pressing the brake pedal.

questions.question: Some air brake systems add alcohol to:

options.text: Stop the brakes from squeaking.
Prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
Keep people from breathing air from the system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator adds alcohol to the brake system to help prevent ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: If your engine catches fire, you should:

options.text: Open the hood right away.
Turn off the engine right away.
Not use a fire extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine right away.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine as soon as possible to stop the fire from spreading. Do not open the hood unless necessary.

questions.question: Which of these surfaces is the most slippery?

options.text: Dry ice
Wet ice
Wet pavement

questions.correctAnswerText: Wet ice
questions.explanation: Wet ice forms when the weather warms just enough to melt the ice slightly. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.

questions.question: A pre-trip inspection should include:

options.text: Checking the engine oil level.
Removing coolant.
Washing the tire rims.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking the engine oil level.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection of the engine, check the oil level, the coolant level in the radiator, and the condition of the hoses.

questions.question: What does it mean if the safety relief valve in the air brake system releases air?

options.text: The compressor needs more air.
The air pressure is too high.
The brakes are working normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air pressure is too high.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air when pressure gets too high. If this happens, something is wrong with the system and a mechanic should check it.

questions.question: How much steering wheel play is allowed?

options.text: 10 degrees.
50 degrees.
75 degrees.

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 degrees.
questions.explanation: A steering wheel should have no more than 10 degrees of play. This equals about two inches of movement at the rim of a 20-inch wheel. More play makes steering difficult.

questions.question: When is emergency equipment, such as fire extinguishers, required?

options.text: Only when transporting hazardous materials.
Only for interstate travel.
In all commercial motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: In all commercial motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must carry appropriate emergency equipment, including fire extinguishers.

questions.question: Do you need to wear a seat belt when driving a truck that requires a CDL?

options.text: No, you do not need to wear a seat belt.
Only if you are carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo.
Yes, you must always wear a seat belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, you must always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: You must wear a safety belt at all times when driving a commercial motor vehicle.

questions.question: What can cause poisonous fumes to enter the cab?

options.text: A broken exhaust system.
Using the wrong fuel.
Not enough oil in the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: A broken exhaust system.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is dangerous. It can allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: When should placards be used?

options.text: Whenever a vehicle is carrying hazardous materials.
When there is extra space on a truck.
Only when carrying more than 200 pounds of hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever a vehicle is carrying hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Placards are required whenever a vehicle carries hazardous materials. A placarded vehicle must display placards on all four sides.

questions.question: Why do large vehicles use air brakes?

options.text: Other brake systems are too loud.
Air brakes work very well.
Other brake systems are hard to find.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air brakes work very well.
questions.explanation: Air brakes are a safe and effective way to stop large, heavy vehicles when used and maintained properly.

questions.question: What should you do before starting a pre-drive inspection?

options.text: The previous inspection report is not important.
Only review the report if passengers will be in the vehicle.
Review the previous inspection report if one exists.

questions.correctAnswerText: Review the previous inspection report if one exists.
questions.explanation: The first step is to review the last inspection report. Only sign the new report if any noted defects have been repaired.

questions.question: What causes the most deaths and injuries in work zones?

options.text: Speeding.
Stopping.
Under-inflated tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding.
questions.explanation: Speeding is the main cause of injury and death in work zones. Always lower your speed when driving through a work zone.

questions.question: What should happen to warning lights and buzzers after the vehicle starts?

options.text: They should stay on for several minutes.
They should turn off within a few seconds.
They should stay on until you turn them off manually.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should turn off within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: Warning lights and buzzers should turn off after a few seconds. If they stay on, something may be wrong with the vehicle.
